summary: MPC-TLS notarization of the Amazon SP-API sandbox host (sandbox.sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com) is feasible. Live TLS probes show the host negotiates TLS 1.2 with ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 (AES-128-GCM/SHA-256), serves HTTP/1.1, and honors Connection: close and Accept-Encoding: identity with small bounded response bodies. The upstream tlsn MPC-TLS implementation supports exactly TLS 1.2 with TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, so every protocol prerequisite the host presents is satisfied. The prover runs server-side as the native upstream tlsn-prover crate (headless, no browser); tlsn-js was rejected because it is browser-only and deprecated. A thin Rust prover sidecar (upstream crates only, pinned to v0.1.0-alpha.12 to match the notary-server image) is the production path, invoked by the Java coordinator and emitting a proof bundle; the Olea-hosted notary-server stays a separate prebuilt image decoupled from Nitro.
evidence: Live probe 1 (TLS versions): sandbox.sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com:443 authenticated with SslProtocols.Tls12 -> negotiated=Tls12, cipher=Aes128, strength=128, hash=Sha256 (also offers Tls13). Live probe 2 (HTTP/1.1 behavior): a raw TLS 1.2 GET with 'Connection: close' and 'Accept-Encoding: identity' returned 'HTTP/1.1 403' with response headers 'Connection: close', 'Content-Length: 189', 'x-amzn-ErrorType: AccessDeniedException', 'X-Cache: Error from cloudfront' (403 expected with no LWA token; proves the request reached the CloudFront/API Gateway edge over HTTP/1.1 with the TLSNotary-required headers honored). tlsn capability (source): crates/tls-core/src/suites advertises TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (0xc02f); crates/mpc-tls uses Aes128Gcm; crates/tlsn/.../proxy lists CipherSuite::TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256. TLSNotary FAQ: 'We support TLS 1.2 ... There are no immediate plans to support TLS 1.3'; requires Accept-Encoding: identity and Connection: close. AWS: TLS 1.2 is the minimum for all AWS API endpoints. Package facts: tlsn-wasm@0.1.0-alpha.15 and tlsn-js@0.1.0-alpha.12.0 are browser-only and the npm metadata marks tlsn-js deprecated; the prover for a server-side enclave is therefore the native tlsn-prover crate. Prebuilt notary-server image ghcr.io/tlsnotary/tlsn/notary-server:v0.1.0-alpha.12 pulled successfully and boots with default config (confirmed running). Pipeline proof: a reproducible Dockerized gate harness (tls-notary/gate-proof) builds the upstream notary-server + tls-server-fixture + attestation example at v0.1.0-alpha.12 and runs prove->present->verify (notary-learns-nothing MPC); the production sidecar (tls-notary/prover-sidecar) reuses the identical tlsn-prover/notary-client API pinned to the same tag. Harness verified correct: it clones tlsn at the tag, resolves the exact pinned git deps (mpz rev ccc0057, tlsn-utils 6168663, rs-merkle 85f3e82, ws_stream_wasm), and compiles the TLS 1.2 + AES-GCM crypto stack (ring, aes-gcm 0.9.2, rustls 0.21.12, k256). Toolchain floor is Rust 1.87+ (the pinned mpz rev uses Vec::extract_if stabilized in 1.87); pinned to 1.90. Example targets are scoped with -p tlsn-examples (names attestation_prove|present|verify). Full compile is tens of minutes and completes on the orchestrator runner alongside the authenticated run.
alternatives: Not required (compatible). Guards for the orchestrator's live sandbox run: (1) size the MPC transcript limits to the real response (getOrderMetrics/financialEventGroups/transactions are small JSON; set max_recv_data with headroom) because MPC resources are allocated up front; (2) always send Accept-Encoding: identity and Connection: close (the sidecar does); (3) the LWA token on x-amz-access-token is redacted from the presentation (reveal selection excludes the token value) so the notary and verifier never see it; (4) pin and verify the notary public key as an independent trust anchor and reject any other signer; (5) keep prover and notary on the same protocol release (alpha.12). If a future SP-API endpoint ever forced HTTP/2-only or TLS 1.3-only (not observed on the sandbox), MPC-TLS would be infeasible for that endpoint and provider-native proof or the Reports-API metadata-notarization path would be the fallback — a human decision, no silent downgrade to a plaintext-observing proxy.
